subject: Agriculture
title: Biocontrol Gone Wrong
description: A fast breakdown of Biocontrol Gone Wrong for builders.

hook.text: Australia introduced cane toads in 1935 to eat beetles. The toads ignored the beetles and became the pest.

buildup.text: 102 cane toads were released in Queensland. Today, 200 million cover northern Australia, eating native wildlife.

discovery.text: Cane toads are poisonous to native predators, who die trying to eat them. Quolls and goannas are vanishing.

twist.text: This isn't unique. Mongoose introduced to Hawaii for rats now prey on endangered birds instead.

climax.text: Modern biocontrol uses host-specific agents tested for decades before release. The cane toad era taught harsh lessons.

punchline.text: Importing a predator without testing is releasing a problem to solve a problem.

quiz.question: Why did cane toad introduction in Australia fail as biocontrol?
options: Toads ignored the target beetles, became invasive, and poisoned native predators
